200: The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a sweet romantic comedy. On his morning train, a high school boy steps in to protect a girl from a groper, then thinks nothing more of it. The girl turns out to be his childhood friend, back in town and grown into the most popular girl at school, and she has never stopped caring about him. It's a gentle, cozy read for fans of slow-burn school romance.
201: The Greatest Demon Lord Reborn as a Typical Nobody by Myojin Katou (Yen Press) is a fantasy action comedy. The Demon Lord Varvatos, tired of being feared and alone, reincarnates thousands of years later hoping for an ordinary life with real friends. He's reborn as Ard Meteor, only to find that magic has declined so far that his everyday abilities are now considered impossible. It's a lighthearted overpowered-hero story for readers who enjoy academy life and big misunderstandings.
202: High School Prodigies Have It Easy in Another World by Riku Misora (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Seven of Japan's most gifted teenagers, including a politician, a doctor, an inventor, and a magician, survive a plane crash and wake up in a medieval fantasy world. Using their modern skills, they set out to change the kingdom that takes them in. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy clever problem-solving and modern know-how in another world.
204: Beauty Pop by Kiyoko Arai (Viz Media) is a lively shojo comedy about hair, style, and rivalry. Kiri Koshiba is a sleepy, offhand girl who happens to be a brilliant hairstylist, though she'd rather nobody knew. Her talent puts her in the sights of the Scissors Project, a group of school heartthrobs who give makeovers, and especially their proud leader, Narumi. It's a bright, funny read for fans of makeover stories and bickering romance.
205: The Magic in This Other World is Too Far Behind! by Gamei Hitsuji (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy action story. Suimei Yakagi is pulled into another world along with his friend, who has been summoned as the hero. Suimei is secretly a modern-day magician, and he quickly finds that his magic, built on real science and study, is far beyond anything this world knows. He just wants to find a way home. It suits readers who enjoy detailed magic systems and a capable, low-key lead.
206: The Mortal Instruments by Cassandra Clare (Yen Press) is a manga-style adaptation of the urban fantasy novels. Fifteen-year-old Clary Fray is at a New York nightclub when she witnesses a murder that no one else can see, committed by teenagers covered in strange tattoos. They are Shadowhunters, warriors who hunt demons, and Clary is about to learn she is part of their hidden world. It's a good fit for fans of the books or readers new to urban fantasy romance.
207: The Record of a Fallen Vampire by Kyo Shirodaira (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action series. Akabara Strauss, the King of Vampires, has spent a thousand years searching for a way to bring back his queen, Stella. Humans and dhampirs alike hunt him, and his quest pulls in old enemies and uneasy allies. It's a moody, dramatic read for fans of vampire stories with sweeping, tragic love at their heart.
208: I Cannot Reach You by Mika (Yen Press) is a tender boys' love romance. Yamato has been in love with his childhood best friend, Kakeru, for years, but he's sure Kakeru only sees him as a friend. Keeping his feelings quiet gets harder as the two grow up and the people around them start pairing off. It's a gentle, heartfelt story for readers who enjoy slow-burn friends-to-lovers romance.
209: Othello by Satomi Ikezawa (Kodansha) is a shojo drama about a girl with two very different sides. Yaya Higuchi is shy and easily pushed around by her classmates, but she has a bold, fearless alternate personality named Nana who comes out when Yaya can't stand up for herself. Yaya doesn't know Nana exists, which leads to plenty of trouble. It's an engaging read for fans of school drama and stories about finding your own voice.
210: I Kept Pressing the 100-Million-Year Button and Came Out on Top by Syuichi Tsukishima (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Allen Rodol is a swordsman with no talent at all, mocked at his academy. Then he finds a strange button that traps him alone in a void for a hundred million years, and he decides to spend all of that time training. He keeps pressing it again and again. It's a satisfying underdog story for readers who love hard work paying off.
211: I Shall Survive Using Potions! by FUNA (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy comedy. After an accidental death, Kaoru Nagase is reborn in another world with one special power: she can create any potion she can imagine, in whatever container she likes. Determined to live quietly and comfortably, she sets out to make her way using her unusual gift. It's a light, fun read for fans of clever, practical heroines and easygoing isekai adventures.
213: Bloody Mary by Akaza Samamiya (Viz Media) is a supernatural shojo story with a dark edge. Bloody Mary is a vampire who has lived for centuries and wants only to die, but nothing can kill him. He believes the young priest Maria Ichiro can, but Maria refuses. Maria has his own problem: he is being hunted, so the two strike a deal, with Mary acting as his bodyguard. It suits fans of moody vampire tales and prickly partnerships.
214: Peach Girl: Change of Heart by Miwa Ueda (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance drama that continues the story of Peach Girl. Momo Adachi's sun-tanned look has always gotten her labeled a party girl, even though she's honest and sweet. Her love life stays complicated, thanks to the two boys she's torn between and a scheming "friend" who never stops making trouble. It's a classic for readers who love high school romance full of twists.
215: Ikigami: The Ultimate Limit by Motoro Mase (Viz Media) is a seinen psychological drama. In a society that claims to teach the value of life, a small number of young adults are chosen at random to die, and they get just 24 hours of warning. Kengo Fujimoto is a government worker whose job is to deliver those death notices. Each story follows one person's final day. It's a thoughtful, often moving read for fans of dystopian drama.
216: Pet Shop of Horrors by Matsuri Akino (Tokyopop) is a supernatural horror series told in short stories. In Los Angeles's Chinatown, the mysterious Count D runs a pet shop that sells rare and wondrous animals, each with a contract that must be obeyed. When customers break the rules, terrible things follow, and Detective Leon Orcot is determined to prove D is behind it. It's an eerie, stylish read for fans of moral fables and dark mystery.
217: Bunny Drop by Yumi Unita (Yen Press) is a warm slice-of-life drama. Daikichi, a thirty-year-old single office worker, goes to his grandfather's funeral and learns the old man left behind a six-year-old daughter, Rin, whom no one in the family wants to take. On impulse, Daikichi offers to raise her himself. It's a gentle, often funny look at learning to be a parent, perfect for readers who enjoy found-family stories.
220: The Witch and the Beast by Kousuke Satake (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy action series. Guideau is a fierce young woman with fangs and a beast's temper, the result of a witch's curse. She travels with Ashaf, a polite, smiling man who carries a coffin, as they track down witches and the trouble they cause. It's a stylish, gothic read for fans of monster hunting, sharp action, and mismatched partners.
221: Inuyashiki by Hiroya Oku (Kodansha) is a seinen sci-fi action story. Ichiro Inuyashiki is an aging office worker whose family ignores him, until an alien accident kills him and rebuilds him as an incredibly powerful machine. He decides to use his new body to help people. A teenage boy changed in the same accident makes a very different choice. It's a tense, emotional read for fans of unusual superhero stories.
222: Ishura by Keiso (Yen Press) is a seinen fantasy action series. The True Demon King, who brought the world to the edge of ruin, is dead, but no one knows who killed him. Now a crowd of monstrously powerful warriors, each a legend in their own right, step forward to fight for the title of true hero. It's a big, bold story for readers who love powerful fighters and dramatic duels.
223: Itazura Na Kiss by Kaoru Tada (DMP) is a classic shojo romantic comedy. Kotoko Aihara, a cheerful but not-so-bright student, finally confesses to Naoki Irie, the school's cold genius, and he turns her down flat. Then an earthquake destroys her house, and she and her father move in with an old family friend, who turns out to be Naoki's father. It's a funny, beloved story for readers who enjoy opposites-attract romance.
224: Tiger & Bunny by Mizuki Sakakibara (Viz Media) is a superhero action comedy based on the anime. In Sternbild City, superheroes fight crime on a live TV show, wearing their sponsors' logos. Veteran hero Kotetsu, known as Wild Tiger, is old-fashioned and past his peak, and he's forced to team up with Barnaby Brooks Jr., a cool, ambitious rookie. It's a fun buddy story for fans of heroes and odd-couple partnerships.
226: Tokyo Mew Mew by Reiko Yoshida and Mia Ikumi (Tokyopop) is a magical girl adventure. While on a date, Ichigo Momomiya is caught in a strange event that merges her DNA with an endangered wildcat. Soon she can transform into a cat-eared superheroine, and she has to find other girls like her to fight aliens who threaten the Earth. It's a cute, upbeat read for magical girl fans of all ages.
227: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Adventure! by Shigekatsu Ihara (Viz Media) is a kids' adventure comedy. Hareta is an energetic boy who grew up in the wilderness, and he sets out to become a Pokémon Trainer with his partner, Piplup. Along the way he meets new friends and rivals in the Sinnoh region and gets caught up in a mystery involving the legendary Pokémon. It's a lively, easy read for young Pokémon fans.
228: Citrus by Saburouta (Seven Seas) is a yuri romance drama. Yuzu Aihara is a stylish, outgoing girl who transfers to a strict all-girls school after her mother remarries. On her first day, she clashes with Mei, the cold and beautiful student council president, only to learn that Mei is her new stepsister. It's an intense, dramatic romance for readers who like their love stories full of tension.
229: Toradora! by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy light novel. Ryuji Takasu is a kind boy with a scary face that makes everyone think he's a delinquent. Taiga Aisaka is tiny, fierce, and known as the "Palmtop Tiger." When the two discover that each has a crush on the other's best friend, they team up to help each other. It's a funny, heartfelt story for fans of school romance.
230: Usotoki Rhetoric by Ritsu Miyako (One Peace Books) is a historical mystery. In early twentieth-century Japan, Kanoko Urabe has the ability to tell when someone is lying, a gift that has made her life lonely. Arriving in the city with nowhere to go, she meets Iwai, a broke young detective who sees how useful her talent could be. It's a charming read for fans of period settings and cozy detective stories.
231: Kiss and White Lily for My Dearest Girl by Canno (Yen Press) is a yuri romance. Ayaka Shiramine works harder than anyone at her school to be the best, yet she can never beat Yurine Kurosawa, a carefree genius who barely seems to try. The two rivals start to see each other in a new light. It's a sweet, gentle series that also follows other girls at the school, great for readers who enjoy soft school romance.
232: Remote by Seimaru Amagi (Tokyopop) is a seinen mystery thriller. Kurumi Ayaki is a cheerful traffic cop who is suddenly assigned to a special unit for unusual crimes. Her new boss, Inspector Himuro, never leaves his basement, so Kurumi becomes his eyes and ears in the field, following his orders by phone. It's a gripping, case-based read for fans of police procedurals.
233: RG Veda by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a sweeping fantasy adventure. Three hundred years after the warlord Taishakuten seized the throne of Heaven, the warrior Yasha-o is entrusted with a child from a fallen clan, Ashura. A prophecy says six stars will gather to change the heavens, and Yasha-o sets out to find them. It's a dramatic, beautifully drawn early CLAMP work for fans of myth-inspired fantasy.
234: Roll Over and Die by Kiki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy drama. Flum Apricot is chosen by the gods to join the hero's party, but her stats are all zero, and her companions see her as dead weight. Betrayed and sold into slavery, she finds a cursed weapon that turns her weakness into strength. It's a tough, emotional read with a lot of heart, suited to older readers who like underdog stories.
235: Sabikui Bisco by Shinji Cobkubo (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure set in a rust-blighted Japan. A deadly Rust Wind is eating away the land, and Bisco Akaboshi, a wanted archer whose arrows grow mushrooms, is searching for a legendary cure. He crosses paths with Milo, a gentle young doctor, and the two set out on a wild journey together. It's a colorful, energetic read for fans of buddy adventures.
237: Wild Ones by Kiyo Fujiwara (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy. After her mother dies, Sachie Wakamura goes to live with the grandfather she's never met, and discovers he's the head of a yakuza family. Her new home is full of tough guys, including Rakuto, the handsome young man assigned as her bodyguard. It's a funny, sweet romance for readers who enjoy an ordinary girl in an extraordinary household.
240: Lord Marksman and Vanadis by Tsukasa Kawaguchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy war story. Tigrevurmud Vorn, called Tigre, is a young earl and a brilliant archer in a kingdom that looks down on the bow. When his side loses a battle, he's taken prisoner by Eleonora Viltaria, one of the powerful warrior women known as Vanadis. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy battles, strategy, and a bit of romance.
242: Yashahime: Princess Half-Demon by Takashi Shiina (Viz Media) is a fantasy action sequel to Inuyasha. Towa and Setsuna are twin half-demon daughters of Sesshomaru, separated as children when Towa is thrown into modern-day Japan. Years later the sisters meet again, along with Moroha, the daughter of Inuyasha and Kagome. It's an exciting adventure for longtime Inuyasha fans and new readers alike.
243: Dragon Goes House-Hunting by Kawo Tanuki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Letty is a dragon, but he's timid, weak, and kicked out of his family's nest. He just wants a safe place to live, so he teams up with Dearia, a powerful elf who happens to be a real estate agent. Together they tour castles, caves, and dungeons looking for the perfect home. It's a gentle, funny read for anyone who likes cozy fantasy.
245: Dreamin' Sun by Ichigo Takano (Seven Seas) is a shojo romance. Shimana Kameko has run away from home after feeling unwanted by her family. She meets a stranger who offers her a room in his house on one condition: she must tell him her dream. Shimana moves in with an unusual group of housemates and starts to find her place. It's a warm, quirky romance for readers who enjoy found-family stories.
246: Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games by Eri Ejima (Seven Seas) is a comedy. At an elite academy for young ladies, Ayaka Shiratori is supposed to be a model of grace and good manners, but she secretly loves fighting games. When she discovers a classmate who shares her passion, their matches get very competitive. It's a fun, silly read for gamers and fans of high-society comedy.
248: Mayo Chiki! by Hajime Asano (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Kinjiro Sakamachi has a problem: being around girls gives him nosebleeds. Then he stumbles on a secret about Subaru Konoe, the handsome and popular butler of the school's richest girl: Subaru is actually a girl. To keep her job, Subaru needs Kinjiro to stay quiet. It's a lighthearted read for fans of school comedies and secret-identity romance.
249: Shimazaki in the Land of Peace by Gouten Hamada (Vertical) is a seinen action drama. Shimazaki was taken as a child and raised as a soldier for an international terrorist group. Now he's living in Japan, trying to build a quiet, ordinary life. His past is never far behind him. It's a tense, thoughtful read for fans of action stories about violence and second chances.
251: Skeleton Knight in Another World by Ennki Hakari (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure. A gamer falls asleep and wakes up in the body of his game character, a heavily armored knight, only to find that under the armor he's a skeleton. Calling himself Arc, he sets out to live peacefully and help people along the way. It's a fun, easygoing story for readers who like a strong, good-hearted lead.
252: Snowball Earth by Yuhiro Tsujitsugu (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action story. Tetsuo is a shy young pilot who, with his giant robot partner Yukio, fought a desperate battle to protect Earth from alien invaders. After the fight, Tetsuo wakes from a long sleep to find the planet covered in ice and his world changed. It's a gripping series for fans of mecha and survival stories.
254: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle by Hiromu (Yen Press) is a school romance drama. Saku Chitose is at the top of his high school's social ladder: handsome, popular, and surrounded by friends. His teacher asks him to help a shut-in classmate who has stopped coming to school. It's a thoughtful youth story for readers who enjoy high school life, friendships, and plenty of witty conversation.
255: Tomo-chan Is a Girl! by Fumita Yanagida (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Tomo Aizawa is a tough, sporty tomboy who's in love with her childhood friend Junichiro. The problem is that Jun has always seen her as one of the guys. Tomo is determined to make him see her as a girl, with plenty of help from her friends. It's a funny, sweet read for fans of short-chapter romance.
259: My Girlfriend's Child by Mamoru Aoi (Seven Seas) is a serious drama about teen pregnancy. A high school couple are very much in love, and after their first time together, the girl discovers she's pregnant. The two teens and their families must deal with the shock and the huge decisions that follow. It's an honest, emotional read for older teens and adults who like realistic stories.
260: Date A Live by Koushi Tachibana (Yen Press) is a romantic action comedy light novel. Spirits, powerful beings from another dimension, appear on Earth and cause disasters. Shido Itsuka, an ordinary high schooler, learns he has the unique ability to seal their powers, but only by making them fall in love with him. It's a funny, action-packed read for fans of harem comedies and sci-fi battles.
261: Reincarnated as a Dragon Hatchling by Necoco (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure. A man wakes up in another world reborn as a newly hatched dragon, alone in a forest full of dangerous monsters. Luckily, he can level up and evolve, and he sets out to grow stronger. It's an entertaining read for fans of monster-reincarnation stories.
263: Kodocha by Miho Obana (Tokyopop) is a shojo comedy. Sana Kurata is a bubbly child actress with a hit TV show and boundless energy. At school, though, her class is run by Akito Hayama, a troublemaker who makes the teachers miserable, so Sana decides to take him on. It's a funny, heartfelt classic that also deals with real family issues.
265: Detroit Metal City by Kiminori Wakasugi (Viz Media) is a seinen comedy. Soichi Negishi is a gentle young man who loves sweet pop music and dreams of singing it. Instead, he ends up as Johannes Krauser II, the frontman of an outrageous death metal band, and he's a huge hit. It's a hilarious, over-the-top read for fans of music and gross-out comedy.
266: Handyman Saitou in Another World by Katsumi Enami (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Saitou was a handyman back home who never felt appreciated for his work. After he's transported to a fantasy world, he joins a ragtag party of adventurers that needs exactly his kind of practical skills. It's a cozy, funny, and sometimes bittersweet read for those who enjoy found-family adventure stories.
268: Imitation by KyungRan Park (Yen Press) is a Korean drama romance. Lee Ma-ha is a member of a struggling K-pop girl group, nicknamed "Imitation" because she looks like a famous star. She works hard to make it, all while getting caught up with the members of a famous boy band. It's an inside look at the K-pop world for readers who enjoy music and showbiz romance.
269: Alice in Murderland by Kaori Yuki (Yen Press) is a dark gothic thriller. The wealthy Kuonji family holds a tea party every month, but this time, the mother makes an announcement: her children must fight each other to the death. Stella, the youngest, is pulled into a dangerous family game. It's a stylish read for fans of Kaori Yuki and twisted fairy-tale fantasy.
270: I'm the Evil Lord of an Intergalactic Empire! by Yomu Mishima (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi comedy light novel. Liam is reborn into a noble family in an interstellar empire, and he plans to live as a cruel, selfish lord. His idea of being "evil," though, keeps making him a great ruler, and his people love him for it. It's a funny read for those who enjoy misunderstandings and space opera.
271: From Far Away by Kyoko Hikawa (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy adventure. Noriko, an ordinary high school girl, is caught in an explosion and finds herself in a strange world. She's rescued by Izark, a quiet swordsman, and soon learns that she may be the "Awakening," a figure whose arrival is prophesied to bring disaster. It's a lovely fantasy romance for fans of classic shojo.
272: The Demon Sword Master of Excalibur Academy by Yu Shimizu (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Leonis Death Magnus, the Undead King, seals himself away to await a prophecy. When he awakens a thousand years later, he's in the body of a ten-year-old boy. Rescued by a girl named Riselia, he enrolls in a school that trains people to fight monsters. It's a fun read for fans of academy fantasy.
273: A Gentle Noble's Vacation Recommendation by Misaki (Yen Press) is a relaxed fantasy adventure. Lizel, a noble, ends up in another world with no idea how to get home. He decides to treat it as a vacation, hiring Gil, a powerful adventurer, as his guide and registering as an adventurer himself. It's a cozy, charming read for those who like slow-paced fantasy.
276: Tying the Knot with an Amagami Sister by Marcey Naito (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy. Uryu Kamihate is an orphan with big dreams of getting into a top medical school. He moves into a shrine run by three sisters, and the condition is that he marry one of them and take over the shrine. It's a fun, sweet read for fans of harem romance.
277: Kill Blue by Tadatoshi Fujimaki (Viz Media) is an action comedy. Juzo Ogami is a top assassin who gets stung by a strange wasp and finds himself back in the body of a junior high student. To find a cure, he has to go to school. It's a funny, action-packed read for fans of Fujimaki and school comedy.
282: See You in My 19th Life by Lee Hye (Ize Press) is a romantic drama. Ban Ji-eum remembers every one of her past lives. In her 19th life, she decides to find Mun Seo-ha, the boy she knew in her previous life. It's a heartfelt, beautiful romance for readers who love stories about fate and lasting love.
283: Steel Angel Kurumi by Kaishaku (ADV Manga) is a sci-fi comedy. Nakahito, a young boy, sneaks into a scientist's lab and accidentally awakens Kurumi, a powerful android girl built as a weapon, with a kiss. Kurumi is now completely devoted to him, much to his embarrassment. It's a silly, lighthearted read for those who enjoy android stories and slapstick comedy.
284: Suikoden III by Aki Shimizu (Tokyopop) is a fantasy war story based on the video game. In the Grasslands, war is brewing between the clans and their neighbors. Young Hugo of the Karaya clan crosses paths with Chris Lightfellow, a famous knight from the opposing side, and both are pulled into the conflict. It's a sweeping story for fans of the game and big fantasy adventures.
287: A Tropical Fish Yearns for Snow by Makoto Hagino (Viz Media) is a gentle yuri slice-of-life story. Konatsu moves from Tokyo to a small seaside town and struggles to fit in. There she meets Koyuki, the quiet, admired president of her school's aquarium club, who has her own reasons for keeping people at a distance. It's a soft, beautifully drawn read for fans of quiet romance.
289: Accel World by Hiroyuki Aigamo (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action manga based on the light novels by Reki Kawahara. Haruyuki Arita is a bullied boy who spends his time in virtual reality. Kuroyukihime, a beautiful student, introduces him to Brain Burst, a program that speeds up thought and turns him into a fighter. It's a solid pick for fans of Sword Art Online.
293: My Boy by Hitomi Takano (Vertical) is a josei drama. Satoko is a successful career woman whose life has taken a lonely turn. One night she meets Mashu, a quiet boy who is neglected at home, and the two begin to spend time together. It's a quiet, thoughtful read for adult readers who like complex relationships.
294: Akira by Katsuhiro Otomo (Kodansha) is a landmark cyberpunk sci-fi story. In Neo-Tokyo, decades after a mysterious explosion destroyed the old city, a teenage biker gang led by Kaneda runs into a secret government project. When Kaneda's friend Tetsuo begins to develop frightening psychic powers, the city starts to come apart. It's a classic for fans of sci-fi, action, and detailed artwork.
295: The Asterisk War by Yuu Miyazaki (Yen Press) is an action romance light novel. Ayato Amagiri transfers to Seidoukan Academy in Asterisk, a city where students fight in battles called Festas. On his first day, he accidentally sees Julis, a princess, changing, and she challenges him to a duel. It's a fun pick for fans of academy battle stories.
296: Golden Time by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Banri Tada has lost his memories in an accident and is starting over as a law student in Tokyo. On his first days of college, he meets Koko Kaga, a beautiful, intense girl with a dramatic entrance. It's a thoughtful, funny read for fans of college romance and the author's Toradora!
297: My Love Mix-Up! by Wataru Hinekure (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy. Aoki has a crush on Hashimoto, but when he borrows her eraser, he sees another boy's name on it, Ida. Things get even more confusing when Ida sees the eraser in Aoki's hand. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of BL and misunderstanding comedy.
298: Aposimz by Tsutomu Nihei (Vertical) is a seinen sci-fi adventure. On a frozen artificial planet, Etherow, a young man, lives with his friends in a small community, training to protect it. When soldiers from a powerful empire arrive, he is pulled into a war and a fight for survival. It's a striking, atmospheric read for fans of Nihei's Blame! and Knights of Sidonia.
